item.title: Hockanum School House in Hadley, Massachusetts
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

About

Built in 1840, this one-room School House served as the educational center for all of the first to eighth grade children in the Hockanum area, later serving only up to sixth grade. This was one of several school houses serving small neighborhood communities around Hadley.

A 1647 Massachusetts law required all towns with 50 or more families to hire a teacher to instruct their children in reading and writing. Parents and students contributed to their school in the form of money, goods, supplies, and chores.

These were one-room schoolhouses, on land that was usually donated. Most schools had one book, the "New England Primer," that was used to teach the alphabet, syllables, and prayer.

The last class to go through this school was in 1933. By then, it was more economical to bus students to the center of town than to keep the neighborhood school houses open.

Along with the outhouse next to it, the Hockanum School House was, and still is, taken care of by the Hockanum community.

item.title: Chile Is Getting a Massive New National Park in 2027
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

If you’ve already hiked the W Trek in Torres del Paine, you may want to start looking a little farther south for your next trip to Patagonia. Chile is planning to establish a new national park in 2027, at the southernmost point of mainland South America, about 40 miles south of Punta Arenas.

In early November 2026, conservation nonprofit Rewilding Chile signed an agreement with the Chilean government to donate an additional 55,186 acres of land toward the creation of Cape Froward National Park (Parque Nacional Cabo Froward). That brings the upcoming park’s total acreage to about 452,000 acres, creating a park 50 percent larger than originally planned when it was introduced in March 2024. For comparison, that’s nearly twice the size of Washington’s Mount Rainier National Park.

item.title: The Hidden Spiegeltent in Chicago, Illinois
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

About

Spiegeltents were made to travel. These round wooden dance halls, lined with mirrors and stained glass, went from fair to fair. They went up fast and came down fast. The one on Randolph Street is not going anywhere. It was built indoors, on the 14th floor of a Loop building.

The building opened in 1926. Rapp & Rapp designed it, with the Oriental Theatre movie palace on the lower floors. The theater is now the James M. Nederlander Theatre. The whole building stands on the site of the Iroquois Theatre, where a fire in 1903 became one of the deadliest in American history.

High above the theater, the architects put a large hall for Masonic meetings. It sat empty for decades. Later it was turned into offices, and a dropped ceiling hid the room completely. When the building was converted into the Cambria Hotel, workers took that ceiling down and found the old hall again, steel bow trusses and all.

In 2019 the tent came over from Belgium in pieces, about 4,000 of them. Belgian tent builders put it together inside the hall, the traditional way, with no nails. It is about 72 feet across. From the hall, it looks like a small circus parked under factory trusses. Inside, there is carved wood, stained glass, velvet and mirrors everywhere. The mirrors are not just for looks. They let guests see around the posts that hold up the roof.

Since October 2026, the tent has been the home of Kermess by Circensia, which kept it right at the center of the room.

Know Before You Go

KNOW BEFORE YOU GO:

The tent is on Floor 14 of the Cambria Hotel Chicago Loop, at 32 W Randolph St. Go in through the hotel and take the elevator up. There are no walk-in visits and no tours. The only way in is with a ticket, booked ahead through Kermess. The current show, Premonitions Inc., is for guests 21 and over. Right next door are the Nederlander Theatre and Couch Place, the alley tied to the 1903 Iroquois Theatre fire.

item.title: Middle East Tourism Has Split. Which Demand Gets Capital?
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Middle East Tourism Has Split.

Skift Take

Gulf travel now runs at two speeds. Pilgrimage and resort demand held through 2026, while long-haul and corporate travel fell away. Every 2027 capital and capacity plan for the region depends on which market an operator underwrites.

Accor’s Duncan O’Rourke told Skift that UAE city hotels cut rates 15% to 20% in August and September to protect occupancy, while Gulf resort and Holy Cities hotels ran ahead of last year. Then the split moved inside Saudi Arabia. After Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s airport in October, 86% of scheduled departures were canceled and Riyadh RevPAR fell 65% to $65 for the month.

For owners, lenders and investors, the 2027 question is which of those markets to underwrite, and on what recovery date.

Hotel Construction Hit a Record as Deals Stalled

Developers kept building. The Middle East hotel pipeline reached a record 771 projects and 188,960 rooms in the third quarter, according to Lodging Econometrics data. Saudi Arabia holds 401 projects, up 15%, and most owners are pushing ahead, though Diriyah canceled a $191 million hotel contract in November. Transactions moved the other way. Knight Frank told Skift that pre-war asking prices no longer match buyer underwriting, and investors are rerunning feasibility studies built on pre-conflict occupancy.

The terms behind that pipeline are changing too. Gulf sovereign funds now expect returns and are phasing projects and selling assets to meet them. Owners are reopening hotel management agreements with operators over performance tests and when management fees get paid. Colliers’ Nicolas Nasra expects the toughest negotiating environment in a decade.

The Recovery Date Sets the Budget

Forecasts disagree by most of a year. Before the October strikes, Accor expected UAE hotels back to pre-war levels by late in the first quarter of 2027. S&P Global Ratings does not expect that before the end of 2027. Since then, Accor has said regional RevPAR may fall about 12% in the fourth quarter, the region’s peak season.

Fourth-quarter results arrive after most 2027 budgets lock in. Every underwriting call made this month carries a recovery date the data cannot yet confirm.

Where the 2027 Call Gets Made

Skift Global Forum East comes to the Grand Hyatt Abu Dhabi on December 9, 2026, with an opening reception on December 8, hosted by Experience Abu Dhabi.

Etihad Group CEO Antonoaldo Neves, Emirates Deputy President and Chief Commercial Officer Adnan Kazim, Rotana CEO Philip Barnes, Minor Hotels’ Amir Golbarg, and leaders from Accor and Radisson will work through these questions with owners and investors placing the same bets.

Complimentary registration is available to approved senior leaders, and standard passes are open to everyone else.

Clarins Family Takes Full Ownership of Luxury Hotel Group Evok

The family behind skincare company Clarins is taking full ownership of Evok Collection, a French owner-operator of five luxury hotels, putting its capital into hotel real estate, brands, and operations.

Famille C Participations, the Courtin family's investment vehicle known as FCP, said Tuesday it's acquiring 100% of Evok's share capital from Zaka Investments, which had been the majority investor. FCP had invested €130 million two years ago for a minority stake.

Price and terms weren't disclosed. Family-owned Clarins produces about $2 billion in annual sales in the skincare industry.
